name: Chagatai Khanate
summary: The Mongol khanate of Central Asia, ruled by descendants of Genghis Khan’s second son Chagatai. Its western half was taken by Timur.

knownFor.label: Chagatai Turkic language
knownFor.note: Became the great literary language of Central Asia, used later by the Timurids and Mughals.

knownFor.label: Silk Road oases
knownFor.note: Samarkand and Bukhara under Mongol rule.

location.value: Central Asia, from the Amu Darya to the Altai mountains.

terrain.value: Steppe, the Tian Shan mountains and the oasis cities of Transoxiana.
terrain.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

climate.value: Continental and dry, with cold winters and hot summers.
climate.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

resources.value: Pasture for herds and the irrigated oases of Transoxiana.
resources.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

disasters.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

population.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

urbanisation.value: Almaliq and Qarshi were royal centres; Samarkand and Bukhara were the great cities.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Chagatai Khanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

disease.value: No specific epidemics are recorded, though the Black Death may have passed through in the 1330s–40s.
disease.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

migration.value: Mongols merged with Turkic peoples and adopted Turkic language.
migration.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

economicBase.value: Herding and taxes on oasis farming and trade.
economicBase.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

tradeRoutes.value: The central stretch of the Silk Road through Samarkand, Bukhara and Kashgar.
tradeRoutes.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.
wealth.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

moneyAndTax.value: Silver dirhams, Kebek’s reformed coins and copper pul.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Chagatai Khanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

inequality.value: A Mongol and Turkic aristocracy ruled over settled oasis farmers and townspeople.
inequality.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

governmentType.value: Semi-elective, later hereditary monarchy with a kurultai.

keyRulers.value: Chagatai Khan (to 1242), Alghu, Duwa (1282–1307), Kebek (1318–1326), Tughlugh Timur (eastern khan, 1347–1363).
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Chagatai Khanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

succession.value: Often fought over by Chagatai’s descendants and powerful emirs.
succession.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

institutions.value: The kurultai assembly of princes chose khans; Mongol law (yasa).
institutions.source: Wikipedia: Chagatai Khanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

stability.value: Split into western and eastern parts in the 1340s.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Chagatai Khanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

eliteConflict.value: Rival khans and emirs; by the 1340s the emirs held real power in the west.
eliteConflict.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

armyAndTech.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

majorWars.value: Wars with the Ilkhanate (e.g. at Herat, 1270) and with the Yuan.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Chagatai Khanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

territoryChange.value: At its largest about 3.4 million km² (around 1310–1350), from the Amu Darya to the Altai.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Chagatai Khanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals: the Yuan dynasty, the Ilkhanate and the Golden Horde; allied at times with Qaidu of the Ögedei line.
alliancesRivals.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

inventions.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

scienceEducation.value: Islamic learning grew after the khans converted.
scienceEducation.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

openness.value: Khans gradually converted to Islam and adopted Turkic language.
openness.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

religion.value: Buddhism and Tengrism until 1326, then Sunni Islam.

languageWriting.value: Middle Mongol, Persian and Chagatai Turkic.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Chagatai Khanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

artsArchitecture.value: Little survives; the Tughlugh Timur mausoleum (14th century) is one example.
artsArchitecture.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

socialStructure.value: Nomadic Mongol and Turkic clans, and city dwellers of the oases.
socialStructure.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

sharedIdentity.value: Descent from Genghis Khan through Chagatai.
sharedIdentity.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

neighbours.value: Yuan, Ilkhanate, Golden Horde, Delhi Sultanate.
neighbours.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

ideasReligions.value: Islam spread among the ruling nomads from the 14th century.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Chagatai Khanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

colonisation.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

riseSignals.value: Chagatai received Central Asia as his share of Genghis Khan’s empire (1227).
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Chagatai Khanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

peakPeriod.value: The early 14th century under Duwa and Kebek.
peakPeriod.source: Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

declineSignals.value: The khanate split into west and east in the 1340s; emirs took power.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Chagatai Khanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

outcome.value: The khanate split in the 1340s: Timur took the west (1363–1370) and the east became Moghulistan, which lasted to 1462 under the Chagatai name.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Chagatai Khanate (checked 6 Nov 2026); Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State (1997)

sources.value: Persian chronicles. Checked against Wikipedia (“Chagatai Khanate”).

overallCertainty.value: Medium. The infobox dates the whole khanate 1227–1347 and its eastern part to 1462; descendants ruled small states much later (to 1680 and beyond). This app uses 1227–1462. Second source: Wikidata ends it in 1687 (last Chagatai rulers); this app follows the eastern khanate to 1462.
